tonight.headline: Jefferson misses a second practice; Warren kicks off at 18:15
body: The bad news got worse since this morning: Justin Jefferson missed Thursday's practice too, and ESPN still projects him at 18.7. A second item is new: D'Andre Swift was added to Chicago's report with a knee and didn't practise, which puts Kyle Monangai, on your bench at 8.4, in play. ESPN has you at 129.4 against Aye-Aye's 125.0, 52%.

Nothing to do today. Jaylen Warren plays at 18:15 with Rico Dowdle out and is already in your lineup. Both open items resolve on Friday's reports: Addison covers Jefferson at 12:35 Sunday, and Monangai is compared with Tuten only if Swift is ruled out.

case.label: The risk
case.body: Jefferson's 18.7 is the number most likely to be wrong in this matchup: two straight DNPs on a sprained right ankle (Vikings.com; A to Z Sports, 1 Oct), and O'Connell still won't talk about the weekend.

case.label: Their side
case.body: Aye-Aye start Herbert (12.6), McCaffrey (20.3), Jeremiyah Love, Kyren Williams, St. Brown, McMillan, Tyler Warren and the Eagles D/ST. McCaffrey was back at practice Thursday after a rest day (49ers Webzone 1 Oct). Nobody on their side plays tonight.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Jefferson practising Friday in any form: then he's a real game-time call rather than a likely absence, and the Addison card stays unarmed until 12:35 Sunday.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Fallback only · check inactives Sun 12:35 Mexico City; the slot locks at 14:05
doFirst.title: If Jefferson is inactive: start Addison in his slot
doFirst.subtitle: Carried from this morning and more likely to fire: Jefferson has now missed two practices.

case.label: The injury
case.body: Right-ankle sprain on his seventh snap against Tampa Bay. DNP Wednesday and DNP Thursday (Vikings.com; A to Z Sports; ClutchPoints, 1 Oct). O'Connell wants him where 'he can go be himself'. ESPN still 18.7: not priced.

case.label: Why Addison, not Coker
case.body: lineup_check.py names Coker (13.0 to Addison's 11.6). Coker was upgraded to limited Thursday with his quad and has 'a shot to suit up' (Panthers.com; SI), but may be a game-time decision, and his inactives come at 16:50, after the Vikings kick off at 14:05. Start a questionable Coker and he sits, and the slot scores zero. Addison is in Jefferson's game and drew 9 targets after Jefferson left in Week 3 (archive).

case.label: The exception
case.body: If Coker carries no designation on Friday's report and ESPN projects him above Addison at 12:35, take the projection and start Coker.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: It fires and Addison scores less than Coker that week.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Fallback only · if Swift is ruled out; both lock Sun 11:00 Mexico City
doFirst.title: If Swift is ruled out: compare Monangai with Tuten
doFirst.subtitle: New this afternoon. Don't move on the news itself; move only if ESPN's new number says so.

case.label: The news
case.body: D'Andre Swift was added to Chicago's report Thursday with a knee injury and did not practise; he wasn't listed Wednesday (Chicago Sun-Times; NBC, 1 Oct). It broke after projections were set: Monangai is still 8.4.

case.label: The role
case.body: Monangai has taken exactly 10 carries in each game, a third of the backfield, behind Swift's two thirds (archive). If Swift sits, Monangai and Roschon Johnson share the extra work (SI Bears 1 Oct), behind a quarterback Chicago hasn't named: Bagent or Keenum.

case.label: The rule
case.body: If Swift is ruled out, ESPN will re-project Monangai. Tuten (12.7) is your lowest starting back and both kick off at 11:00. Start whichever the projection then prefers; inside two points it's a coin flip, and the projection still decides.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: It fires and the back you bench outscores the back you start.

doFirst.sources: Chicago Sun-Times · NBC · SI Bears · Week 1–3 archive

whatWentWrong.title: Jefferson has missed two practices and the projection still hasn't noticed
whatWentWrong.lead: 18.7 before Wednesday, 18.7 now. That gap is why the Addison card exists.

case.label: The evidence
case.body: Vikings Thursday report: DNP (ankle), second day running (Vikings.com; A to Z Sports 1 Oct). No new quote from O'Connell beyond 'not in any place right now to talk about what that means for the weekend'.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Any practice Friday and a questionable tag: then it's a 12:35 Sunday check. A doubtful or out tag Friday: start Addison and stop waiting.

whatWentWrong.title: Swift's knee is new, and this morning's Bears quarterback line was wrong
whatWentWrong.lead: It's Bagent or Keenum, not Keenum or Caleb Williams. And Swift's knee, new Thursday, makes Monangai the one bench back whose number could jump.

case.label: The correction
case.body: Caleb Williams (Grade 2 hamstring) hasn't practised and is on track to miss a second game; the choice is Tyson Bagent or Case Keenum, and Ben Johnson says it's made but won't announce it (Heavy 30 Sep; Bleacher Nation 1 Oct).

case.label: What it changes
case.body: Monangai came off the list of possible drops this afternoon: he was the named drop on the Meyers watch row. The Monangai card above is the other half.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Swift practising Friday with no designation: the card never arms and Monangai is a sixth back again.

worthALook.name: Jakobi Meyers
worthALook.lead: One game of a new role, and limited again with a thumb.

case.label: The role
case.body: 8 touches and 19.4 points in Week 3 (archive), when Brian Thomas Jr. played 23 snaps. Coen put that down to 'a little bit more 12' personnel, not a benching (NBC 29 Sep), which corrects the 'benched for drops' line this row has carried since Tuesday. Meyers was limited Wednesday and Thursday with the thumb (Jaguars.com 1 Oct).

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: 3 and 1 touches in Weeks 1–2 (archive). One week, and the waiver tool says nothing on the wire clears this roster's bar.

case.label: When to act
case.body: Seven-plus targets again at Cincinnati with Thomas still part-time. The drop would be Addison once Jefferson is healthy, not Monangai.

worthALook.name: Ka'imi Fairbairn
worthALook.lead: The kicker comparison: a free agent, still only 0.5 better. Hold Pineiro.

case.label: The comparison
case.body: ESPN: Fairbairn 9.3 (free agent), Pineiro 8.8, Shrader 8.5, Carlson 8.4. Fairbairn isn't on Houston's report; Shrader (groin) was a full participant and Steichen says he 'should be fine' (Yahoo 1 Oct).

case.label: What would change it
case.body: A roster seat opening this week; the Pineiro thesis says it goes to the kicker if one does.

doNotChase.name: Kalif Raymond
doNotChase.lead: The wire's biggest riser, dropped by Bok-aneers this morning, and nobody knows who's throwing to him.

case.label: The rise
case.body: He leads Chicago's receivers with 19 catches and 214 yards, five-plus targets every game, 6 of 7 for 90 and a score in Week 3 (Sporting Tribune 29 Sep). The rise is production; I found no role change behind it.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: He projects 10.0, below Addison (11.6) and Coker (13.0) on your bench, and the waiver tool didn't surface him. Chicago's quarterback is Bagent or Keenum, unnamed. He's on waivers until Saturday 01:00.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Jefferson ruled out for more than this week: then a receiver seat matters, and Chem claims cost nothing lasting.

doNotChase.sources: Sporting Tribune · Bleacher Nation · ESPN activity log

doNotChase.name: Jaylen Wright
doNotChase.lead: Still rising, and he's the man splitting Gordon's work.

case.label: The rise
case.body: Limited Wednesday and Thursday with the foot, and listed ahead of Gordon on Miami's depth chart since Achane went to IR (Yahoo 1 Oct; Vikings.com report).

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: He'd be your sixth back, splitting a Miami backfield you already own half of, at Minnesota, who allow the 4th-fewest points to RBs (footballdb).

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Wright takes over outright in Week 4 (Gordon under 8 touches): then the Gordon claim is the thing to revisit, not a reason to own both.

doNotChase.lead: Limited again with a back injury, and the fit is still wrong.

case.label: The rise
case.body: 7-105-1 with Mason Taylor out; Taylor DNP again Thursday. Sadiq limited both days with his back (NewYorkJets.com 1 Oct).

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: Chem starts one tight end and the flex is RB/WR only. Likely isn't on the Giants' report.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Likely on a Giants injury report.

waiverAnalysis.summary: Nothing on the wire beats this roster on usage, from three weeks of data, which is still thin. Same answer as this morning. The weakest movable players are Monangai and Addison, and Monangai is off the table while Swift's knee is unresolved.
